scenes.title: Tally × Envio
scenes.vo: Tally, for the best use of Envio.

scenes.title:
History can't come
from the RPC.
scenes.sub: Monad's public RPC rejects eth_getLogs beyond ~100 blocks.
scenes.vo: Tally's receipts, family top-ups and points all need history. But Monad's public RPC rejects log queries beyond about a hundred blocks. So the history comes from Envio.

scenes.title:
From a tap
to a receipt.
scenes.vo: Here is the whole path. A payment in the app becomes a Monad transaction. HyperSync streams the block, our HyperIndex handler turns the Paid event into a Payment row, and the app reads it back over GraphQL.

scenes.title: Riya pays $4.50.
scenes.sub: The agent picks the cheapest oat latte; Monad settles it.
scenes.vo: Riya pays four fifty for an oat latte. The transaction settles on Monad in under a second.

scenes.title: Paid → Payment.
scenes.vo: Our handler listens for the Paid event, writes a Payment with the item, price, cosign flag and transaction hash, and rolls it into the merchant's and the allowance's totals.

scenes.title:
Same tx hash.
Indexed.
scenes.sub: The hosted HyperIndex returns the payment Riya just made.
scenes.vo: Seconds later the hosted indexer returns that same payment. Same transaction hash, same price, with the family top-up right beside it.

scenes.title:
Receipts, points,
family top-ups.
scenes.sub: Every list in Tally is read from Envio.
scenes.vo: And it's back in the app. Receipts, this week's spend, family top-ups, points and the café's sales are all read from Envio.

scenes.title:
Deployed from
our repo.
scenes.vo: The indexer is deployed on Envio Cloud straight from our repository.

scenes.title: Tally controls the item.
scenes.vo: Tally. Every payment, on the record.
